# Offline four-port collective collector

Repair and extend the supplied C collector and its replay pipeline. This is a
finite CPU packet replay, not a live transport or a hardware reproduction.
The observable contract is the wire transcript and retained collector state.
The provided C switch and packet codec are the working substrate; the Python
entry point, wire utility and C ABI are editable too. A replacement may use any
provisioned offline language, provided the same entry point and behavior work.

## Request and numerical domain

One UTF-8 JSON object, allowing surrounding JSON whitespace, has `cases`, a list of 0–8 independent cases. An empty batch returns {"cases":[]}. A case has
`primitive` (allreduce, reduce, broadcast, barrier, allgather, reducescatter),
`mode` (2 or 3), `root` (0–3), `segments` K (1–2^20), `words` D (1–1024),
`capacity` N (1–4096), `start` (0–2^24−1), `events` (an array of event objects), and optional `trace` (0–32,
default 0). Barrier instead requires D=0,K=1. Reducescatter requires K divisible
by four. N may exceed K. No state crosses cases. All numerical fields are
integers, not booleans or floats. Vector arithmetic is unsigned modulo 2^32;
wire words use big endian. JSON objects have no duplicate keys or nonfinite
numbers. Every object has exactly its documented required and optional keys. Missing or
extra keys, wrong types, unknown names, and any stated bound violation are illegal.
Validate the entire batch first; illegal requests return exactly {"error":"invalid"},
exit status zero, without partial results or compilation. Invalid UTF-8/JSON,
duplicate keys, trailing values and input longer than 4 MiB have the same reply.
`request.py` is the public format-only validator; it contains no collector logic.
There are at most 65536 event objects across a batch. Unknown fields are absent.

Logical input sequence p lies in [0,K). The 24-bit physical PSN is
(start+p) mod 2^24. Every receiver has its own logical output sequence q and
physical PSN (start+q) mod 2^24. ACKs are cumulative: wire PSN a acknowledges
prefix length (a−start+1) mod 2^24. Only a strictly increasing prefix no larger
than that receiver's successfully sent prefix at packet arrival is effective; every other ACK is
ignored. This includes ACK zero, stale, future and unsolicited ACKs. These
sequence spaces never span a half-turn, including the 3K gather output space.

## Collective values and output spaces

For each p, a contribution from each required source is retained once; later
copies never replace its value. Allreduce, reduce, reducescatter and barrier
require all four sources. Broadcast requires only root; data from other ranks
is invalid. Gather also waits for all four sources at p before any of that
p's output is ready. No partial-gather forwarding is part of this contract.

| Primitive | Output records belonging to input p |
| --- | --- |
| allreduce | sum of four vectors to each rank, q=p |
| reduce | sum to root only, q=p |
| broadcast | root's unchanged vector to each nonroot, q=p |
| barrier | empty payload to all four ranks, q=0 |
| allgather | each source s's unchanged vector to every d≠s, q=3p+ord(d,s) |
| reducescatter | sum to d=floor(p/(K/4)) only, q=p mod (K/4) |

ord(d,s) is s's zero-based position in ascending ranks with d omitted.
A destination's new output records have increasing q, without gaps. A complete
later input cannot bypass an incomplete predecessor in that destination's
output space. Sending does not imply acknowledgment.

## Retention, ACK ownership and transport pressure

The retired prefix b starts at zero. New data can occupy only logical p in
[b,min(K,b+N)); data at p≥b+N is blocked, and data at p<b is stale. Neither can
allocate or overwrite a slot. Within the admitted range the first occurrence
of each (p,source) is accepted; another occurrence is a duplicate, including a
copy carrying a different valid payload. Admission and DATA classification use b at packet arrival; later service never
retries a packet just classified as blocked. Slot identities are logical p, not
merely p mod N. Incomplete, completed, sent and unacknowledged records all
consume the same bounded pool.

For each source r, R[r] is its longest contiguous received prefix. Non-sources
in broadcast have prefix zero. An upstream ACK may cover only a contiguous
received prefix whose contributions are safe:

* Mode 3: accepted contributions are safe immediately, including incomplete
  collective inputs. The collector owns subsequent result retransmission.
* Mode 2: an allreduce/barrier contribution from r is safe after receiver r's
  result ACK; reduce requires root's result ACK; broadcast requires all three
  receivers; reducescatter requires that p's mapped receiver; gather requires
  all three receivers of that source's value at their mapped output PSNs.

The eligible upstream prefix E[r] is the largest such prefix, at most R[r].
The last successfully sent upstream prefix U[r] starts at zero. Zero-length
upstream ACKs are never sent. A received duplicate or stale DATA requests a
repeat of the currently eligible ACK to its source; it does not itself request
a result retransmission. A repeat request persists until an ACK succeeds.
A retired p must be complete, have every required output acknowledged, and
have U[r]>p for every required source. b is the longest prefix satisfying these
conditions. Payloads remain intact until retirement, including gather values
whose first transmission has succeeded. Upstream progress alone cannot free
storage, even in mode 3.

A transport budget initially permits unlimited successful emissions. A budget
of n≥0 permits n further emissions, then rejects attempts until changed. A
failed attempt emits no bytes, advances no sent prefix, and ends that service
opportunity immediately. Earlier successes remain effective. This models
local egress backpressure, not packet loss reported by a NIC.

After every endpoint-valid input packet, and on flush/retry, the observable
emission priority is: eligible pending upstream ACKs in ascending rank; then
(on retry only) the selected receiver's previously sent but unacknowledged
results in ascending q; then new results in ascending destination rank and q.
Pending upstream ACK means E>U or a repeat was requested, with E>0.
A failed result retransmission does not queue a continuation: a later retry
starts again at the then-current downstream acknowledged prefix. New-result
backlog and upstream ACK repeat requests remain pending as described. No result
retransmission changes the new-output sent prefix. Empty/blocked/duplicate/
stale/ignored-ACK opportunities still permit pending service. Wire-invalid or
endpoint-invalid frames are simply dropped and do not trigger service.
Retirement reflects all successful work from that opportunity, even if a
later send fails. No automatic timer, ACK reception or fair drain is implicit.
Unfinished inputs and permanent loss are valid finite traces.

## Frame acceptance and canonical output

Frames contain Ethernet, IPv4 without options, UDP, BTH, optional AETH, payload,
and four-byte ICRC; no Ethernet FCS/padding is present. All multibyte fields
except ICRC are network byte order. A wire-valid frame has exactly its IPv4
length plus 14 bytes, IPv4 version/IHL 0x45, protocol 17, a valid header checksum,
and the flags/fragment-offset field is exactly 0x0000 or 0x4000 (DF only). UDP length equals IPv4 length−20,
both ports are 4791 and UDP checksum is zero. BTH opcode is DATA 0x04 or ACK
0x11, flags/padding byte zero, pkey 0xffff, QPN top byte zero; APSN top byte is
0x80 for DATA and zero for ACK. DATA payload length is exactly 4D. ACK body is
exactly four bytes: top byte 0x1f, low 24 bits equal (wire PSN+1) mod 2^24.
Its payload is not a vector. All lengths and ICRC must agree. Other IPv4
TOS/TTL/ID values are unrestricted on ingress. Wire validity is checked before
endpoint validity: a frame failing both is counted only as wire-invalid.

ICRC is standard reflected CRC32 (polynomial 0xedb88320, initial/final XOR
0xffffffff), stored little endian. Its input is eight 0xff bytes followed by
the IPv4 datagram excluding ICRC, with IPv4 TOS, TTL and checksum bytes replaced
by 0xff, UDP checksum bytes by 0xff and QPN's top byte by 0xff. This checksum
rule is also implemented by the format-only `wire.py` utility.

For ingress port r: host MAC=02:00:00:00:00:(r+1), switch
MAC=02:01:00:00:00:(r+1), host IP=10.0.0.(r+1), switch IP=10.0.0.(101+r),
host QPN=0x100+r, switch QPN=0x200+r. A wire-valid ingress must have that
host/switch as source/destination and target the switch QPN. DATA also needs
a required source and logical p in [0,K); otherwise it is endpoint-invalid.
ACKs from nonreceivers are endpoint-valid but ignored by the prefix rule.

Output reverses MAC/IP endpoints and targets host QPN. Canonical output has
IPv4 TOS=0, ID=0x1111, DF=1, TTL=64; all remaining bytes follow the acceptance
rules above with fresh IPv4 checksum and ICRC. DATA carries the specified
collective payload and ACK carries the cumulative eligible input prefix.

## Event encodings

`wire.py:emissions` is format expansion only, not the collector algorithm.
Missing optional event fields take the defaults below. Events run in list order.

* `data`: rank, p; optional count=1, step=1, seed=0, values, xor=[]. It expands
  count packets at p+i*step in that order; all p must be in [0,K). Counts are
  1–2^20. Step is an integer in [−2^20,2^20] and may be zero. With values, count=1 and values is
  exactly D unsigned 32-bit words. Otherwise word j (j=0,…,D−1) is
  (seed+0x9e3779b9*(p+1)+0x85ebca6b*(rank+1)+0xc2b2ae35*(j+1)) mod 2^32.
  Seed is unsigned 32-bit. xor is a list of [byte_offset,xor_byte] pairs applied
  sequentially after sealing the frame; offsets are integers in [0,57+4D],
  bytes are integers in [0,255], and each pair is exactly a two-element list.
  Checksums are not recomputed after xor.
* `ack`: rank, upto (0–3K+1), one canonical ACK with PSN start+upto−1 modulo
  2^24. It does not imply any DATA or successful delivery.
* `wire`: rank, hex, an even-length ASCII string of only 0–9/a–f/A–F (empty allowed), decoding to
  0–4154 bytes. This can express invalid headers, endpoints and ACKs.
* `budget`: n, either −1 (unlimited) or 0–2^31−1, replaces remaining allowance;
  it performs no service. `flush` has no other fields and requests ordinary service.
* `retry`: rank, requests repeating its eligible upstream ACK, if any, and all
  of that receiver's sent/unacknowledged results, with the priority above.
* `snap`: tag, a UTF-8 string of 0–64 bytes (unpaired surrogates are illegal), records the current certificate
  without service. Duplicate tags are allowed and retain their order.
* `train`: p, count, width (1–N), ranks (a permutation of 0,1,2,3), optional
  reverse=false (a JSON boolean), seed=0 (unsigned 32-bit). Count is 1–2^20
  and 0≤p<p+count≤K. This is a compact traffic generator. It partitions
  [p,p+count) into consecutive chunks of at most width. In each chunk, DATA is
  generated in ranks order and then ascending p (descending if reverse), with
  the same payload formula. Broadcast skips nonroot sources. After the chunk
  come ACKs in rank order for all output positions belonging to inputs below
  the chunk's end: upto=end for ordinary receivers, 0 for nonreceivers, 3*end
  for gather, and clamp(end−r*K/4,0,K/4) for scatter. These ACKs are ordinary
  input packets and may be ignored. Train never retries blocked input.

Across the batch, expanded replay work is at most 2^20 units: one per generated
or raw wire packet, budget or flush; one additional unit per applied DATA xor
pair per generated packet; N per snap; 12N+4 per retry. Train's DATA and
four ACKs per chunk are charged individually. A second static traffic budget
is 256 MiB: four times each ingress frame's byte length, plus (12N+4)*(4D+62) per
retry, plus N*(16D+32) per snap; budget/flush cost zero bytes. Rank is always an integer 0–3. Every event is exactly the fields listed above,
including `op`; flush has only `op`. Event lists may be empty. Raw wire corruption,
DATA from a nonroot broadcast port and ignored ACKs are legal replay events, not
illegal JSON requests. These bounds
permit million-packet diagnostics while accounting for gather replication,
retained-window inspection and retransmission fanout. They bound expansion,
not correctness by elapsed time. The 120-second batch budget includes compilation.

## Response certificate

Return exactly `{"cases":[certificate,...]}` in request order. Each certificate
has exactly state, buffer, wire_sha256, packets, bytes, snapshots and trace. `packets`
and `bytes` count successful egress frames and their lengths. `wire_sha256` is
SHA256 of their concatenation, each prefixed by destination rank as one byte
and frame length as a four-byte little-endian integer. Empty transcript uses
SHA256 of empty bytes. `trace` contains up to the first requested number of emissions,
each `{"rank":r,"hex":lowercase_frame_hex}`; no failed attempt appears.
`snapshots` contains, in snap order, objects with tag plus state, buffer,
wire_sha256, packets and bytes at that point. Snapshots do not include trace.

`state` is exactly 32 nonnegative integers, indexed from zero:
0 retired prefix b; 1 occupied slots; 2–5 received prefixes R; 6–9 new-output
successfully sent prefixes; 10–13 downstream acknowledged prefixes; 14–17
successfully sent upstream prefixes U; 18 accepted-endpoint DATA packets;
19 accepted-endpoint ACK packets; 20 successful DATA emissions; 21 successful
ACK emissions; 22 newly accepted contributions; 23 duplicates; 24 blocked
DATA; 25 stale DATA; 26 wire-invalid frames; 27 endpoint-invalid frames;
28 ignored ACK packets; 29 failed send attempts; 30 slot overwrites (must be
zero); 31 reserved (zero). DATA classifications 22–25 are disjoint and total
18. Invalid frames contribute neither 18 nor 19. Every wire input has exactly
one of these endpoint-valid or invalid classifications.

`buffer` is a 16-digit lowercase hexadecimal FNV1a64 digest (offset
14695981039346656037, multiply by 1099511628211 after XORing each byte, modulo
2^64). Include occupied slots in increasing logical p. For each fold p as
8-byte little endian, source mask as one byte, and complete flag as one byte.
Then fold: for gather, rank order presence byte and, when present, its 4D raw
network-order bytes; for broadcast its 4D raw bytes; for other primitives,
the D current aggregate words as unsigned 4-byte little endian. Barrier adds
no payload bytes. Presence and completeness describe accepted input, independent
of result transmission. Retired/unused storage is omitted. The empty digest is
cbf29ce484222325. No allocator addresses or timing enter any certificate.

# Execution profile

The collected artifact is the ordinary source tree `/workspace/project`, at most
8 MiB and 256 entries, with `build` and `__pycache__` directories excluded.
Other ordinary files are permitted. Entries must be regular files/directories,
without symbolic links or hard links. The UTF-8 entry point `solver.py` is at
most 256 KiB. Artifact files and runtime are read-only during scored replay.
It executes as `python3 -I -B /workspace/submission/solver.py`; it may build and
load C code in scratch. Python is 3.11.14, Linux x86-64. C11 GCC and GNU make,
binutils and libc development headers are provisioned. The exercised local
compiler is GCC 9.4.0; the public Debian image provisions its distribution GCC.
The exercised local worker pairs GCC9 with a matching read-only link SDK; it
does not replace the replay runtime libc. The public Debian image provisions
its matching compiler/libc development packages together.
The implementation must use only the supplied offline runtime and dependencies.
Each invocation gets one whole JSON batch. Input is at most 4 MiB; stdout at
most 32 MiB, stderr at most 1 MiB. Stdout must contain exactly one JSON object;
empty/malformed/nonfinite/incorrect output or a nonzero exit fails. Correct
output followed by explicit `os._exit(0)` is supported. Normal text, `.buffer`,
`fileno()`, raw descriptors 0/1 and `os.fdopen` are supported.

The local execution profile uses an unprivileged UID in an allowlisted chroot.
The runtime and submission are read-only. `/workspace/tmp` is writable, empty
at the start of each invocation and removed afterward. No other writable path
is provided by that local profile. `/proc` and `/sys` are not mounted.
The runtime includes `/dev/null`, `/dev/zero`, `/dev/random`, `/dev/urandom`.
Maximum wall time is 120 seconds per whole batch; per-process CPU soft/hard
limits are 180/181 seconds; virtual address space is 2 GiB per process;
processes/threads are limited to 64 per UID; open descriptors to 256 per process;
each file to 64 MiB; core files to zero. No CPU affinity is imposed. The replay needs only a single computation thread; build jobs are capped at two. Timing is a feasibility bound, not a
score or an uncontended-host performance claim.

Local worker syscall restrictions: sockets/socketpair/connect; System V shared
memory/semaphores/message queues; kill/tkill/tgkill/ptrace; process_vm_readv/writev;
unshare/setns/mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot; setsid/setpgid; UID/GID/groups changes;
open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at; bpf; keyctl/add_key/request_key;
perf_event_open/userfaultfd/io_uring_setup/enter/register; pidfd_getfd are denied
with EPERM. clone3 returns ENOSYS. clone namespace flags masked by 0x7e820000
are denied with EPERM. Other fork/clone/thread creation may work within the UID
limit. Non-x86-64/x32 syscall ABIs are killed. Privileges cannot be gained.
Environment is fixed: PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, HOME=/workspace,
LANG=LC_ALL=C, TMPDIR=/workspace/tmp, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1,
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, PYTHONHASHSEED=0; BLAS/OpenMP thread variables are one.
Network access is disabled. No GPU, switch, NIC access or external services.

Scratch has a sampled emergency brake at 1 GiB of summed max(logical size,
allocated blocks) or 50000 directory entries, including the scratch root;
sampling is approximately every 0.25 seconds. Crossing this brake invalidates
that local run as an infrastructure error with no score. This is not an exact
storage quota: open-unlinked files, inode counts and aggregate resources are
not hard-capped by cgroups on the current local host. Keep temporary use small.
Formal Harbor/container isolation, aggregate quotas, image layers and artifact
transport require separate infrastructure validation; local runs do not certify
those properties.

`python3 public_check.py project/solver.py` is an unprivileged development checker for
ONLY the published examples. It seals the entry-point file bytes in a Linux memfd and actually executes a
bounded child with the numeric limits above, inherited container/worker network
and syscall policy, and no hidden inputs. A trusted loader inside the child supplies an ordinary
`__main__`, `__file__`, `sys.argv[0]` and the project import directory; stdin/stdout remain real OS streams. The rest of the project is read from its ordinary paths. The isolated local worker freezes the complete project read-only before the development check; in an ordinary container the development user owns their editable source tree.
The public fixture invocations share the enclosing worker scratch directory;
the trusted outer worker clears that directory around the whole public check.
The authoring local adapter caps the entire public-check command at 180 seconds,

command produces no score. It refuses execution as host root.
Run it inside the public container or the maintainer's isolated local adapter.
